svg.text: K3b PASSIVE TOOLS ON THE BELT CASSETTE — the belt moves the food, the tools stay
Every tool rests on the cassette side plates; the hand only places, lifts or turns it. No gates, no motors in the tools.
driven roller Ø 70 × 300: 30 Nm by the hand roll axis = 850 N
gauge ramps rise 1 : 10 → 10 mm of roller x = 1 mm of gap
knife drawn ±50 mm in y, 2 mm in front of the Ø 22 nose
tools: roller, doctor blade, curl frame, comb, gauge plate, envelope
1 DRIVEN ROLLER ON THE GAUGE RAMPS (sheeting)

g.text: the hand sets the roller further toward the nose
→ lower on the ramp → thinner sheet
The hand turns the roller at belt speed by its roll axis (30 Nm);
the press force goes into the side plates, not into the hand.
Heights ×3. Dough 20 → 4 mm in 6–8 passes; pasta 1.2 mm.
flap: salted, dusted with flour (sifter cup)
A 12 g spoon of mustard lies on the slice; the belt draws
the slice under the still blade: an even 1 mm layer.
The camera measures the slice, the hand lifts the blade.
filling stripe at the leading edge
top view: plough wings fold the sides 15 mm
Bread-moulder principle: the edge curls up the hood and back,
the Roulade forms between moving belt and still hood (Ø 45–50).
The camera stops the belt with the flap at 5 o’clock.
7 blunt blades at 32 mm pitch; also divides dough strips.
Next (not shown): the roller at 22 mm presses the pieces flat.
Belt pushes the roast to the gauge (stall at 5 N); 4–15 mm slices.
6–8 s per slice; juice runs to the nose into the tray.
→ each slice overlaps the last by 30 %
→ a cutlet is laid down flat
Fixed nose; the hand moves plate, tray, pan or cradle under it.
Shingled roast slices, flat Schnitzel, patties, pizza.

svg.text: Belt runs toward the nose (left) · tools rest on the cassette side plates, so their forces stay in the cassette · orange = placed or moved by the hand
